data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims the record is underdetermined because there is no experiment 'varying only the test while holding mutations fixed.' This misreads the attachment's evidentiary structure. The problem supplies a controlled natural experiment: compile.py is singled out as 'shown-to-fail-first installation,' while every other module is 'ordinarily-guarded.' The mutations are therefore pre-stratified by the very property the question asks about — whether the test constrained its subject — not randomly scattered across described and undescribed paths as SRC_001 asserts. The record does not leave the causal variable unmeasured; it labels the group where the constraint was deliberately installed versus the groups where it was not. SRC_001's demand for an independently generated mutation set is satisfiable in principle, but its premise — that the existing distribution is merely a 'joint product of test strength and mutation placement' with nothing to distinguish the groups — ignores that the attachment itself provides the distinguishing factor. The question asks what the compile.py anomaly and the 4/4 to 6/7 baseline jointly reveal about constraint conditions; SRC_001 refuses to infer any condition and thereby treats the 'shown-to-fail-first' installation procedure as epistemically inert, even though that procedure is the only thing in the record that makes the 1/9 loss informative rather than noisy.
